alternate_names: TTD Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Venkatapalem
deities: Anjaneya Swamy (shrine under construction as part of the TTD expansion project)

history.summary: The Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple at Venkatapalem, on the banks of the Krishna River in the Amaravati region, is the principal Venkateswara shrine of Amaravati town. Consecrated in 1983 and managed by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), it was built as a Tirumala-inspired temple for devotees of the Amaravati-Guntur-Vijayawada belt who cannot always travel to Tirupati. The temple follows classic Dravidian architecture with carved pillars, prakarams and a gopuram, and observes traditional Vaikhanasa Agama rituals similar to Tirumala, including daily Suprabhatam, Thomala and Archana sevas and TTD-style laddu prasadam. In 2019 the TDP government resolved to develop the temple on about 25.4 acres on the Krishna banks, and in November 2025 Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu performed boomipujan for a Rs. 260-crore expansion in two phases: phase one adds a second prakaram, a seven-storey Raja Gopuram, Arjitha Seva Mandapam, Addala Mandapam, Vahana and Ratha Mandapams, an Anjaneya Swamy shrine and a pushkarini; phase two adds mada streets, an Annadanam complex, pilgrim accommodation, priest quarters, an administrative building, a meditation hall and parking. The project is targeted for completion in about two and a half years.

name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Amaravati is an ancient town on the right bank of the Krishna River in Palnadu district, once the capital of the Satavahanas. It is a dual pilgrimage centre: home to the great Buddhist stupa (built around 200 BCE in the Ashokan era, with panels of the Buddha's life and Jataka tales), the 125-foot Dhyana Buddha statue, and the Amaravati Heritage Centre; and to the ancient Amareswara Swamy temple, one of the Pancharama kshetras. The town also lies within the modern Amaravati capital region of Andhra Pradesh.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (approx. 30-50 km; commonly cited as ~50 km from the temple; taxis available).
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction (major railhead, approx. 25-35 km; about 45 minutes to 1 hour by road) or Guntur Junction (approx. 35 km).
travel.road: Well connected by road; APSRTC buses and private taxis run from Vijayawada (approx. 25 km) and Guntur (approx. 35 km) to Venkatapalem/Amaravati.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather is pleasant and cool. Brahmotsavam, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Sri Krishna Janmashtami are the most vibrant times to visit, though more crowded; early mornings on weekdays are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify locally - timings may extend during festivals). General darshan is free; specific sevas and special darshan tickets carry charges. Modest dress required; footwear and cameras/phones are generally not allowed inside the sanctum.
